name: All-in-One Utilities
author: wordtenance

sections.description:
All-in-One Utilities replaces a handful of small, single-purpose plugins with one well-built toolkit. Every feature is off until you switch it on, each has its own help text, and nothing loads on your site unless you use it.

Users

  • Username Updater: change a user’s username, which WordPress normally doesn’t allow, and optionally email them about it.
  • Multiple User Roles: give one user several roles at once, such as Editor and Shop Manager.
  • Custom User Avatar: let users pick an avatar from the Media Library instead of relying on Gravatar.
  • Switch to User: see the site exactly as another user does, then switch back in one click.
  • Users Screen: ID, Registered, Account Age and Last Login columns on Users → All Users.

Login page

  • Your own logo, background color or image, and a message on the login screen.
  • Choose which links it shows and where users land after logging in or out.
  • Reword the login, registration, lost-password and reset-password forms.
  • Preview every login screen while you’re still logged in.

Security

  • Hardening: switch off XML-RPC, the file editor, user enumeration, application passwords and the REST API for visitors.
  • Limit Login Attempts: lock a device out for a while after too many wrong passwords.
  • Author Pages: stop author archives listing everything a user published and revealing their username.
  • Works behind a proxy or CDN: choose where the visitor’s IP address is read from.

Media

  • Default Featured Image: a fallback image wherever a post has none.
  • Require Featured Image: stop posts being published without one, or with one that’s too small.
  • SVG Uploads: allow SVG logos and icons, cleaned of anything that could run code.

Admin

  • Show IDs on posts, pages, media, users, comments and terms.
  • Hide Dashboard widgets and the Welcome panel for everyone.
  • Your own admin footer text, a hidden WordPress version, and the toolbar hidden for chosen roles.

Performance

  • Stop loading emoji, embeds, the block library, Dashicons and other files your pages may not need.
  • Clean the page head: generator tag, RSD and WLW links, shortlinks, feed links, version strings.
  • Switch off comments or RSS feeds across the site, slow down or stop Heartbeat, and limit revisions.
  • Turn off the random content redirects WordPress 7.2 adds (/random/ and ?random), or keep them for the archives you choose.
  • Use the classic editor, control automatic updates, and add accessibility fixes such as a visible focus and a skip link.

Content and duplicates

  • Duplicate Posts & Pages: copy a post or page, with its terms, custom fields and featured image, as a new draft.
  • Duplicate post finder: find posts with the same title, choose which copy to keep, protect posts that must never be removed, and run the scan on a schedule with an email report.
  • Duplicate Menu: copy a navigation menu to try changes safely.

Custom code

Add CSS and JavaScript to the front of your site, and CSS to wp-admin, in a proper code editor with syntax checking.

Emails

  • Set the sender name and address for every email your site sends.
  • Send a test email.
  • Switch off or reword the emails WordPress sends to administrators and users.
  • Email Log: keep a searchable record of every email your site sends, from any plugin.

WooCommerce

Country States: state and province dropdowns for the countries WooCommerce has no list for. This tab only appears while WooCommerce is active.

Tools

  • Import and export settings between sites.
  • Reset any settings tab, and undo the last reset.
  • Database Cleanup: revisions, spam, expired transients and other leftovers.
  • A System Report to send with support questions.

Premium add-ons

The free plugin is complete on its own and never requires an add-on. These optional paid add-ons from WordTenance add more features to the same screens:

  • All-in-One Utilities Pro: site branding (colors and typography), two-factor login, a custom login URL, SMTP and branded emails, user management, media folders, custom post types, code snippets, performance and developer tools.
  • Woo Add-on: WooCommerce cart rules, checkout fields, conditional payments and shipping, custom order statuses, reward points, abandoned cart recovery and stock alerts.
  • Tools Add-on: download any plugin or theme as a ZIP, roll plugins back, and back up automatically before every update.
  • Chat: ask what any setting does and jump straight to it, from a chat panel on every admin screen.

Prefer to have it set up for you? Use All-In-One Utilities → Request Setup to ask WordTenance for an estimate.

Documentation and support

Full documentation with screenshots is at wordtenance.com/docs. For help, use the support forum here or the System Report screen inside the plugin.
sections.installation:
1. In wp-admin, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin and search for “All-in-One Utilities”, or upload the plugin’s zip file there.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Open All-in-One Utilities in the admin menu and switch on the features you want under Settings. Nothing changes on your site until you do.
sections.faq:
I used version 1.x. Will my settings carry over?

Yes. Version 2.0 is a complete rewrite, and on the first page load after the update it copies your 1.x settings across: the features you switched off, the default featured image, Username Updater and Multiple Roles. Afterwards everything is under All-in-One Utilities → Settings.

Will it slow my site down?

No. Each feature’s code only runs when that feature is switched on, and most of them make your pages lighter, not heavier.

Is it a caching plugin?

No. The Performance tab removes things WordPress loads that many sites don’t need. It works alongside whichever caching plugin you use.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

When you deactivate it, the plugin asks whether to keep or delete its settings and data for when you delete it later. Keeping is the default. Your posts, pages, media and users are never touched.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Each site has its own settings.
sections.changelog:
2.2.0

  • New: Disable Random Content (Settings → Performance). WordPress 7.2 adds /random/ addresses and ?random links that redirect visitors to a random post. Turn them off, or keep them for chosen category, tag, taxonomy or post type archives, optionally only for some terms. Author archives always stay off, so usernames aren’t revealed. Permalinks are rebuilt automatically. Has no effect before WordPress 7.2.

2.1.1

  • Fix: Country States no longer makes the UK County (or any state field WooCommerce shows as optional) required when “Make the state required” is on.
  • Fix: Country States data cleaned up: duplicate state names removed (Bahamas, Luxembourg, Madagascar, Marshall Islands, Vietnam and Russia), “Sverd” corrected to Sverdlovsk Oblast, and the 14 missing Russian regions added (83 in all).
  • New: Country States adds Kosovo’s 7 districts.
  • Declares compatibility with WooCommerce’s High-Performance Order Storage and the Cart and Checkout blocks. Tested with WooCommerce 11.3.

2.1.0

  • New: Request Setup. Ask WordTenance to install and configure the plugins for you (All-In-One Utilities → Request Setup).
  • New: one License page for every add-on’s license key.
  • About now lists every feature of each plugin, where to find it in wp-admin, and has a search box.
  • Settings sections remember whether you opened or closed them, and open or close with a click on their heading.
  • Wide tables scroll sideways instead of overflowing.
  • Fix: emails no longer fail when WordPress’s default sender address is invalid (for example on localhost); the site’s admin email is used instead.
  • Fix: SVG uploads with escaped CSS no longer need PHP’s mbstring extension on WordPress older than 7.1.

2.0.0

  • A complete rewrite by WordTenance, with a new settings screen organized into tabs, search and built-in help.
  • Settings from 1.x are carried over automatically.
  • New: Custom User Avatar, Switch to User, Users screen columns.
  • New: login page branding and texts.
  • New: Limit Login Attempts, Author Pages and Visitor IP settings.
  • New: Require Featured Image and SVG Uploads.
  • New: admin customization (IDs, Dashboard widgets, footer, toolbar).
  • New: Disable Comments, Disable Feeds, Classic Editor, Update Control and Accessibility.
  • New: Duplicate Posts & Pages, the duplicate post finder and Duplicate Menu.
  • New: Custom Code, email settings, Email Log and WooCommerce Country States.
  • New: import/export, settings reset, Database Cleanup and a System Report.
  • Choose whether to keep or delete the plugin’s data when you deactivate it.
  • Requires WordPress 6.6 and PHP 8.2 or later.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
